questions.prompt: You give an image model two reference images. What should the prompt do?

options.text: Say what each image is for, such as "the sneaker from image 1 on the street from image 2".
options.explanation: Right. Google's template for combining images gives each image a role.

options.text: Say nothing about them. The model will work out which image is the product and which is the scene.
options.explanation: Without roles the model guesses which image is the product and which is the scene.

questions.prompt: A logo on a reference image must not change. Which sentence helps most?

options.text: "Make it look good, with a nice mood and a great overall feel for the brand, please. Use any style you like."
options.explanation: This does not name anything to protect.

options.text: "Add the logo from the second image. Keep its three leaves and shape completely unchanged."
options.explanation: Right. Google advises describing critical details and saying that they remain unchanged.

options.text: "Add the logo, but be creative with it and give it a fresh new look on the shirt. Use new colours for it."
options.explanation: Asking for creativity invites changes to the logo.

questions.prompt: A result looks close to your reference. What is the right next step?

options.text: Compare it with the original file, since brand elements can drift across generations.
options.explanation: Right. A reference helps but does not promise an exact copy.

options.text: Assume it is exact, because it used a reference and the reference was correct. Skip the check.
options.explanation: OpenAI's limits list says the model may struggle to keep brand elements consistent.

options.text: Delete the original file to avoid confusion between the two versions of the logo.
options.explanation: You need the original to compare and to place the exact logo later.
